profile.campus: Espoo, Finland (Equinix HE6, part of Equinix's Helsinki-region cluster)
profile.reading:
This is Equinix's HE6 facility at Sinimaentie 12 in Espoo, Finland, a short distance from sibling facility HE7, part of a cluster of Equinix buildings, HE3 through HE7, that the company markets collectively under its Helsinki region heading. Equinix's own dedicated page describes HE6 as a five-story, reinforced-concrete building with 1,756 square meters, about 18,901 square feet, of colocation space, N+1 power and cooling redundancy, generator autonomy of 30 hours or more at full load, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, and a 99.9999%-plus global uptime guarantee, though it does not publish a specific IT capacity figure in megawatts or kilowatts. Equinix entered the European colocation market through its 2007 acquisition of IXEurope and expanded further through its 2015 acquisition of TelecityGroup for about $3.8 billion, though Equinix's current HE6 page does not attribute the building to either predecessor company by name. Equinix, founded in Silicon Valley in 1998, converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX; the company's own about page states a current global footprint of 281 data centers across six continents, while Wikipedia separately cites approximately 260 data centers across 33 countries as of 2025.

As an EU-based facility, this data center falls under the European Union's Energy Efficiency Directive reporting requirements, which since 2024 have required data centers above a minimum capacity threshold to report power usage effectiveness, water usage, and other sustainability metrics to a European Commission database, part of a broader EU push for standardized data center energy transparency that does not have a direct equivalent in most of the US markets covered elsewhere in this registry.

Finland has positioned itself as a Nordic data center hub in part due to its naturally cool climate, which reduces cooling energy costs, and its access to renewable hydro and wind power from the broader Nordic electricity grid; several other major operators beyond Equinix, including Google and Microsoft, have also built large-scale data centers in Finland citing similar climate and clean-power advantages.
